topic: Raw salads off the plate for a doctor stuck on laxatives
angle: A 'healthy' food can be the wrong food for your gut right now; a doctor who knew the theory needed someone to look at his actual plate

story_structure.situation: Man in his late 40s, a doctor himself. On laxatives for a month, sleeping 5.5 to 6 hours, fat loss stalled after three years of dieting.
story_structure.task: Get his gut moving on its own and his sleep back before chasing more fat loss. He knew the theory; the gap was what he was actually doing.

hook: He's a doctor, and he had been on laxatives for a month. The first thing I took off his plate was salad.
draft:
He's a doctor, and he had been on laxatives for a month. The first thing I took off his plate was salad.

He was in his late 40s and had been dieting for three years. His weight had stopped moving. He was sleeping five and a half to six hours a night. He knew the theory of gut health better than most of my clients.

The task wasn't more fat loss. It was getting his gut working on its own again, and getting his sleep back.

So for the first two to three weeks we left fat loss alone. Raw salads and raw vegetables came off his plate. Meals came at set times. Training was capped at five days a week.

He stopped the laxatives from the start of the plan. By day 10, his bowels were moving on their own almost every day. The sleep score he gave himself went from 2 to 7.

His weight went up by about 4 kg. After three years of eating less, his body was refilling its carbohydrate stores, and those hold water. That's not fat.

The lesson: "healthy" food is whatever your gut can handle right now. For him, at that point, raw salads were part of the problem.

If you're eating clean and your gut keeps getting worse, look at what's on your plate before you add anything new.
final:
He's a doctor, and he had been on laxatives for a month. The first thing I took off his plate was salad.

He was in his late 40s, three years into dieting, and his weight had stopped moving. Most nights he slept five and a half to six hours. He knew the theory of gut health better than most people I coach. What he needed was someone to look at what he actually ate every day.

For the first two to three weeks we put fat loss aside and worked on his gut and his sleep. Raw salads and raw vegetables came off his plate, meals moved to set times, and training was capped at five days a week.

He didn't use laxatives at all once the plan started. Within ten days his bowels were moving on their own almost every day, and the sleep score he gave himself went from 2 to 7.

His weight went up by about 4 kg. After three years of eating less, his body was refilling its stored carbohydrate, and that store holds a lot of water along with it.

Raw salads are good food for plenty of people. For his gut, at that point, they were making things harder.

If you're eating "clean" and your gut keeps getting worse, look at what's already on your plate before you add something new.

#GutHealth
